name: Compressed Biogas (CBG): Blending Mandate & Waste-to-Gas Plant Builders
scope: India's CBG Blending Obligation on city-gas CNG/PNG (3% FY27 rising to 5% FY29), the plant build-out and pipeline bottleneck, and the listed builders, integrated producers and gas utilities exposed to it.

summary.one_line: The mandate is running ahead of supply. H1 FY27 blending was 1.7% against a 3% FY27 target, and only a small share of the ~210 working plants connect to a pipeline. Listed exposure is real but small: SFC (CBG EPC/technology), TruAlt (CBG ~2.5% of revenue) and Oriana (approvals only). Most of these stocks are down 10-62% over the past year.
key_points: CGD entities sold 115.9 MMSCM of CBG in H1 FY27 (Apr-Sep 2026) against 6,800 MMSCM of CNG plus domestic PNG. That is 1.7% blending. Reaching the 3% FY27 obligation needs 408 MMSCM, so 292.1 MMSCM must come in Oct-Mar (S2).

Delivered FY26 blending was about 0.9% against the 1% first-year obligation: 111.48 MMSCM of CBG on 12,033 MMSCM of CNG/D-PNG (S3). Required CBG supply rises to 1.03, 1.54 and 2.07 MMSCMD in FY27, FY28 and FY29 (S3).

Supply is constrained by pipeline access, not just plant count. 210 functional plants run at an average of 44% capacity, while pipeline-linked plants run at 65-69% (S2). PNGRB counts only 36 connected plants of 210, and 133 functional plants (1,661 TPD) have no pipeline plan (S1). Of 308 plants under construction, 247 have no connectivity plan (S2).

The Rs 23,731 cr GOBARdhan scheme (guidelines Sep 2026) fixes the CBG price at Rs 2,110/MMBTU (~Rs 98/kg) until at least March 2036. It gives Rs 1.25 cr/TPD capital aid plus up to Rs 0.75 cr/TPD for aggregation and manure equipment, capped at Rs 30 cr per project. From year 2, contracts carry 90% take-or-pay for the CGD buyer and 50% supply-or-pay for the producer (S4).

SFC Environmental (listed 3 Nov 2026) is building 125 TPD Tinsukia and 300 TPD Bhubaneswar waste-to-CBG plants worth Rs 501.7 cr combined, with 10-year O&M (S6). Management says 'we are not an EPC contracting company', describes a JV/technology model, and guides FY27 EBITDA margin to 18-20% against a historical 29-30% (S7).

TruAlt's CBG unit Leafiniti earned Rs 42.84 cr in FY26 (S10), against Rs 1,728 cr consolidated sales (S20), so CBG is about 2.5% of revenue. Management cites 60-70% CBG EBITDA margins and ~250 TPD with partners over 3-4 years (S9). The Sumitomo JV's first Mudhol unit was reported delayed (S12).

Gas utilities are moving from MoUs to JVs. Gujarat Energy (ex-Gujarat Gas) seeks partners for 200 TPD (S15). IGL signed an MoU with CEID for 25+ plants and 125+ TPD (S17). MGL signed a 350 TPD Mankhurd concession with BMC (S18). GAIL is building a Rs 123 cr, 300 TPD-feedstock plant in Bengaluru (S19).

There is little sign the theme is priced in. One-year returns are -62% for Oriana (S21), -28% for TruAlt (S20), -28% for DCM Shriram (S22), -26% for IGL (S23), -19% for Praj (S25) and -10% for MGL (S24). SFC closed listing day at Rs 426.10 against a Rs 330 issue price (S5).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Technology/EPC-plus-O&M suppliers with orders in hand. SFC has Rs 501.7 cr of CBG orders with 10-year O&M (S6), commissioning expected in March (S7).

Producers with captive feedstock and existing offtake, if fixed pricing (~Rs 98/kg to 2036) and take-or-pay contracts hold (S4). TruAlt (press mud and grain by-products) and DCM Shriram (sugar by-product CBG at Ajbapur) fit this (S9, S14).
Gas utilities that secure CBG early lower their compliance risk. Pipeline-linked plants run at 65-69% utilisation against a 44% average (S2), so utilities that connect plants get more gas per rupee.

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: CGD entities face a steep H2 FY27 catch-up: 292.1 MMSCM needed in six months after 115.9 MMSCM in H1 (S2). None of the sources consulted spell out a penalty beyond the contract take-or-pay terms (S4).
Sub-scale, cascade-dependent plants. Cascades carried 65.7% of offtake and pipelines only 8.9% in FY26 (S3). Average plant utilisation is 44% (S2).
Margin dilution for builders. SFC's H1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 6.8% (S6) against 28-29% in its IPO-period financials (S5).
New entrants face execution slippage. TruAlt's Sumitomo unit was delayed (S12), and Oriana's 110 TPD is approved, not under operation (S13).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: PNGRB H2/full-year FY27 CBG blending data against the 408 MMSCM requirement (S2).
TruAlt's delayed Sumitomo JV units and the six Leafiniti-GAIL 12 TPD plants (S11, S12).
Gujarat Energy's CBG JV EOI, which closes 15 Dec 2026 (S15), and IGL/MGL definitive JV agreements (S17, S18).
Q3 FY27 results: watch SFC's solid-waste margin and TruAlt's CBG utilisation (S7, S9).

subsections.title: What the CBG Blending Obligation is

blocks.text: City gas distribution (CGD) entities must source a share of their CNG (transport) and domestic PNG volumes as compressed biogas. The share was 1% in FY26, and rises to 3% in FY27, 4% in FY28 and 5% from FY29 (S3, S4). Delivered FY26 blending was about 0.9%, or 111.48 MMSCM of CBG on 12,033 MMSCM of CNG/D-PNG (S3). In H1 FY27 it rose to 1.7% (115.9 of 6,800 MMSCM), still well short of the 3% FY27 level (S2).

blocks.text: Organic feedstock (segregated or mixed municipal waste, press mud and sugar by-products, agri residue, cattle dung) goes through anaerobic digestion. The raw biogas is purified to ~95% methane, then compressed into cascades or injected into a CGD pipeline. Fermented organic manure (FOM/LFOM) is a by-product. GAIL's Bengaluru design turns ~300 TPD of organic MSW into ~12.6 TPD of CBG and ~21.6 TPD of FOM (S19). Note that waste-plant 'TPD' figures (e.g. SFC's 125/300 TPD) are usually feedstock throughput, not CBG output (S6, S19).

blocks.caption: Disclosed plant costs (capex per TPD derived by this report)
columns: Implied Rs cr per TPD CBG

blocks.text: Revenue side: the GOBARdhan guidelines fix CBG at Rs 2,110/MMBTU (~Rs 98/kg at 95% methane) until at least March 2036. Capital aid is Rs 1.25 cr/TPD for new plants plus up to Rs 0.75 cr/TPD for aggregation and manure equipment, capped at Rs 30 cr per project (S4). Illustration (derived): a 12 TPD plant at Rs 98/kg grosses ~Rs 43 cr a year at full output on a 365-day basis, or ~Rs 19 cr at the 44% average utilisation PNGRB reports (S2). Maximum subsidy (~Rs 24 cr) covers roughly 20-29% of the ~Rs 7-10 cr/TPD capex seen above. TruAlt management cites 60-70% EBITDA margins in CBG (S9); this is a company claim, not a sector benchmark.
Utilisation drives the economics. Pipeline-linked plants run at 65-69%, against a 44% average (S2), so connectivity can matter more than the subsidy.

subsections.title: What changed in the last three months

items: GOBARdhan scheme guidelines (reported 22 Sep 2026): Rs 23,731 cr outlay over 2026-27 to 2035-36, five existing schemes subsumed from 1 Sep, applications open until 31 Dec 2030 (S4).

Producers may seek offtake for up to 100% of saleable CBG. Year 1 carries no penalty; from year 2 the CGD buyer must take at least 90% of nominated quantity and the producer must supply at least 50% (S4).
Affordability support is capped at Rs 10/kg (Rs 215.31/MMBTU). There is a Rs 625 cr credit guarantee and a Rs 500 cr CBG Ecosystem Challenge Fund (S4).
Pipeline support covers 50% of CGD-link cost, up to Rs 50 lakh/km for steel or Rs 7.5 lakh/km for MDPE, over up to 75 km, for plants of at least 2 TPD (S4).
The FY27 obligation stepped up to 3% from April 2026, and H1 delivery reached 1.7% (S2).

subsections.title: Supply build-out and the pipeline bottleneck

blocks.text: In FY26, cascades (truck-mounted cylinders) carried 65.7% of CBG offtake and pipelines only 8.9% (S3). This edition could not confirm the ~838 registered-plant figure in the brief from any source opened, so it is not used.
The sources do not give a stated penalty for a CGD entity missing the blending percentage. The only enforceable terms found are the contract take-or-pay and supply-or-pay clauses (S4).

blocks.text: SFC's model: the brief describes SFC as EPC/owner. Management told analysts 'we are not an EPC contracting company, we are a technology business'. It described CBG JVs where SFC earns technology supply, O&M, gas sales and returns on its ~12.5% project equity (half of a 25%-equity-funded JV). Mumbai Deonar and other projects depend on JVs, DPR approval and land handover, and some would execute over 2028-2030 (S7). The ~Rs 7,000 cr pipeline is not secured (S7). The client is described as a 'public sector oil marketing company' in the results release (S6) and as Oil India on the call (S7). The order book was Rs 1,656.17 cr, of which solid waste was Rs 419 cr (S6). H1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 6.8% (S6), against IPO-period FY26 EBITDA of Rs 235.81 cr on Rs 821.27 cr total income (S5).

TruAlt: H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 1,437.98 cr (+243%) with PAT of Rs 94.27 cr. Q2 PAT fell to Rs 34.99 cr on high maize prices (S8). The investment case is still overwhelmingly ethanol (2,000 KLPD) (S8). Management guides to ~20-24 CBG plants and ~250 TPD with partners over 3-4 years (S9).

blocks.text: Market-cap coverage: listed CBG pure-plays are all small-cap (SFC, TruAlt, Oriana SME). Large and mid caps (GAIL, IGL, MGL, Gujarat Energy, DCM Shriram) carry CBG as a minor line item or compliance cost. The edition found no genuine listed mid-cap pure-play.

items: Broker coverage that groups these stocks as a 'CBG theme' was not found in this edition. Available analysis is mostly concall summaries and trade press.
Perivis (SFC Q2 call summary): flags FY27 margin guidance of 18-20% as below the historical 29-30%, and the CBG pipeline as forward-looking and not secured (S7).
Sovrenn (TruAlt Q2 call summary): records management's 60-70% CBG EBITDA claim and ~250 TPD build-out ambition, with feedstock moving to grain-based operations (S9).
QCIntel reported TruAlt's Sumitomo CBG JV delayed (26 Oct 2026) (S12). The full article is paywalled, so the length of the delay could not be confirmed.

blocks.text: No buy/sell views or price targets are given here. Management guidance above is a company forecast.

items: Connectivity: 247 of 308 under-construction plants have no pipeline plan (S2), and cascade logistics dominated FY26 offtake (S3).
Utilisation and feedstock: the 44% average utilisation (S2) suggests feedstock and offtake friction. TruAlt halted sugar-based plants on feedstock cost (S9).
Subsidy is milestone-linked, not upfront (S4), which can delay cash for new entrants.
Builder margins: SFC's H1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 6.8% (S6), and solid-waste blended EBITDA was ~10% in H1 (S7).
Execution: TruAlt JV delays (S12); Oriana's projects are approvals only (S13).
Enforcement: no explicit penalty for missing the CBO was found (S4).

blocks.text: The earliest earnings link is SFC: its CBG orders are in revenue now through solid-waste EPC and convert to 10-year O&M (S6, S7). TruAlt's CBG ramp matters at the margin but remains ~2.5% of revenue (S10, S20). For utilities, the H2 FY27 catch-up need (292.1 MMSCM) is a cost and compliance issue rather than an earnings driver (S2).

companies.name: SFC Environmental Technologies
companies.role: Wastewater/solid-waste technology firm. Through a subsidiary it is building 125 TPD Tinsukia and 300 TPD Bhubaneswar waste-to-CBG plants (Rs 501.7 cr) with 10-year O&M (S5, S6), and positions itself as a technology/JV partner rather than an EPC contractor (S7).
companies.impact: The most direct listed CBG builder. Commissioning is expected in March and the Deonar/JV pipeline runs to 2028-30, but CBG work is diluting margins (FY27 guide 18-20% vs 29-30% historical) (S7).

companies.name: TruAlt Bioenergy
companies.role: 2,000 KLPD ethanol producer in Karnataka (S8). Its Leafiniti arm runs CBG, with a Sumitomo JV and a 51:49 GAIL JV for 6 x 12 TPD plants (S11).
companies.impact: CBG was ~2.5% of FY26 revenue (Rs 42.84 cr of Rs 1,728 cr) (S10, S20). Management targets ~250 TPD with partners (S9), but the first Sumitomo unit slipped (S12).

companies.name: Oriana Power
companies.role: Solar EPC/BOOT company (S21) with GOBARdhan approval for five 22 TPD CBG projects (110 TPD, Rs 750 cr) in UP, Gujarat, MP and Maharashtra via wholly owned subsidiaries (S13).
companies.impact: An option on CBG with no operating capacity yet. The stock is down 62% over one year (S21).

companies.name: DCM Shriram
companies.role: Commissioned a 12 TPD CBG plant at its Ajbapur sugar unit on sugar-process by-products, 27 Mar 2025 (S14).
companies.impact: A line item against Rs 13,538 cr FY26 sales (S22). It benefits from the fixed CBG price but is not a theme driver.

companies.name: Praj Industries
companies.role: BioEnergy segment supplies CBG technology and turnkey plants. Its board approved up to Rs 100 cr for a CBG JV with BPCL (S25).
companies.impact: Technology supplier positioned for plant orders. CBG revenue is not separately disclosed; stock down 19% over one year (S25).

companies.name: Gujarat Energy (formerly Gujarat Gas)
companies.role: Largest CGD by volume. Renamed effective 14 May 2026 after the GSPC/GSPL merger (S16). Its EOI seeks JV partners for 200 TPD of CBG (S15).
companies.impact: Obligated buyer building supply to meet 3-5% blending. Small capex (~Rs 100 cr) relative to the group (S15).

companies.name: Indraprastha Gas
companies.role: Delhi-NCR CGD. JV MoU with CEID for 25+ CBG plants and 125+ TPD (S17).
companies.impact: Compliance-driven buyer. The disclosure is an MoU; no JV company, investment amount or locations have been disclosed yet (S17).

companies.name: Mahanagar Gas
companies.role: Mumbai CGD. Concession agreement with BMC for phase I of a 350 TPD Mankhurd CBG plant (S18).
companies.impact: Securing municipal-waste CBG supply. SFC links Deonar projects to JV/DPR/land approvals over 2028-30 (S7).

companies.name: GAIL (India)
companies.role: Building a Rs 123.42 cr Bengaluru plant processing 300 TPD of MSW into ~12.6 TPD of CBG, with offtake by GAIL Gas (S19). Holds 49% of TruAlt's Leafiniti (S11).
companies.impact: Large-cap where CBG is immaterial to earnings but sets cost benchmarks and supports partners.

companies.name: Oil India
companies.role: Named on SFC's call as the client for the Tinsukia and Bhubaneswar CBG projects, paying in ~45 days (S7).
companies.impact: Its PSU payment record lowers receivable risk for SFC (S7). CBG is negligible for Oil India itself.

method: First edition, researched 28 Nov 2026 with web search and page fetches. Policy and volume data come from PNGRB material, read directly where possible and otherwise via news reports citing PNGRB, plus GOBARdhan guideline coverage. Company facts come from exchange-filing coverage, IPO data, results releases and concall summaries. Market cap and 1-year returns are from Screener.in (27 Nov close); 3- and 6-month returns were not available from sources opened, and the dashboard shows live numbers. Capex per TPD and revenue illustrations are this report's own arithmetic on cited inputs. Claims that could not be confirmed (the ~838 registered plants, the SFC-MGL 1,000 TPD Deonar JV, TruAlt's Rs 65 cr per plant, DCM Shriram plant cost) are left out or flagged. No ratings or price targets.

cbg_plant_developers: Companies building or running compressed biogas plants, including EPC/BOO players, as evidenced by commissioned plants, orders or approved projects
integrated_ethanol_agri: Producers adding CBG to existing ethanol, sugar or chemical sites using by-products and residue as feedstock
gas_utilities_offtake: Obligated CNG/PNG distributors that must meet the blending target and are buying, partnering in or building CBG supply
